Why Measure Growth
• Student learning is a central goal of
 education
• Assessments of student achievement
 provide evidence of current status of
 student knowledge and understanding
• Learning is demonstrated by growth in
 student achievement from one point in time
 to a another point in time – not by status at
 either point time alone

Uses of Growth Measures
• Informing students, parents, and teachers about
 individual student progress
 – Measuring individual student growth can be useful, but
 utility is limited due to low reliability of individual
 student gain scores
• School accountability systems
 – Growth measures have substantial advantages over
 status measures for accountability
 – Unlike status measures, growth takes prior
 achievement into account

Growth vs. Value Added
• Value-added models attempt to make
 causal attributions
• Growth measures are purely descriptive
• In the absence of random assignment
 causal attributions are always suspect and
 subject to challenges (see, for example,
 Raudenbush, 2004; Rubin, Stuart &
 Zanutto, 2004)
